In addressing the inexact setting of the single-stage problem, we derive an overall complexity bound, improving the dependence on the dimension compared to the existing results for the centralized SMPECs.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadjavad Ebrahimi, Uday V. Shanbhag, Farzad Yousefian

item.title: Variational Properties and KL Exponent of Square-Transformed Polyhedral Composite Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2506.10110v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider one of the most common reparameterization techniques, the square transformation. Assuming the original objective function is the sum of a smooth function and a polyhedral function, we study the variational properties of the objective function after reparameterization. In particular, we first study the minimal norm of the subdifferential of the reparameterized objective function. Second, we compute the second subderivative of the reparameterized objective function on a linear subspace, which allows us to fully characterize the subclass of stationary points of the reparameterized objective function that correspond to stationary points of the original objective function. Finally, utilizing the representation of the minimal norm of the subdifferential, we show that the Kurdyka-\L ojasiewicz (KL) exponent of the reparameterized function can be deduced from that of the original function. Applications to concrete optimization models are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Wenqing Ouyang

item.title: Efficient Online Mirror Descent Stochastic Approximation for Multi-Stage Stochastic Programming
item.description: arXiv:2506.15392v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the unconstrained and the minimax saddle point variants of the convex multi-stage stochastic programming problem, where consecutive decisions are coupled through the objective functions, rather than through the constraints. We approach the problems from the infinite-dimensional policy perspective, but consider an online setting where only the policies corresponding to the actual realization of the underlying stochastic process are needed. This leads to a tractable formulation, where the dimension of the output is linear in the number of stages $T$. We propose hypothetical Mirror Descent Stochastic Approximation (MDSA) for the infinite-dimensional policies using stochastic conditional gradients. By taking advantage of the decomposability of the updates across stages and realizations of the underlying stochastic process, we show that the proposed MDSA algorithms admit efficient online implementation. In the moderate-accuracy regime, where the allowed total error scales linearly with $T$, the oracle complexity is linear in $T$ and the extra space needed is independent of $T$.
item.dc:creator: Junhui Zhang, Patrick Jaillet

item.title: Learning from the past in an irreversible investment problem
item.description: arXiv:2508.21731v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider an irreversible investment problem under incomplete information, where the investor decides whether and when to make investments in a project. Upon investment, the investor acquires previously hidden information from the project's past (''learning from the past''), and so the learning rate of the problem is controlled by investing. We set up this original problem as a recursively defined stopping problem with a learning-from-the-past effect. We show that, under general conditions, at each recursion step there exists a one-sided stopping boundary. We proceed to present the optimal investment strategy as a sequence of semi-explicit stopping boundaries derived from the smooth fit conditions of the corresponding free-boundary problems. Feasibility of our approach is then demonstrated by solving example boundaries numerically and by performing sensitivity analysis with respect to different model parameters.
item.dc:creator: Topias Tolonen-Weckstr\"om

item.title: Spare Strategy Analysis and Design for Mega Satellite Constellations Using Markov Chain
item.description: arXiv:2509.09957v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper presents a Markov-chain-based method for the early-phase analysis and design of spare-management architectures for large-scale satellite constellations. To assess the long-run viability of such concepts of operations, satellite failure and replenishment processes are modeled as Markov chains and analyzed through their stationary solution. We reinvestigate an indirect spare strategy, modeled as a multi-echelon periodic-review reorder-point/order-quantity policy, in which spares are first delivered to parking orbits and then transferred to constellation planes. The stock levels in constellation and parking orbits are each modeled as independent Markov chains, and a fixed-point iteration yields a consistent joint stationary solution that describes the strategy's average behavior. This approach accurately captures the stochastic interplay within a multi-echelon model driven by orbital mechanics, avoiding the aggregation assumptions of prior works and remaining valid across a wider operating domain. Building on this fast, accurate analysis, we formulate an optimization problem and solve it via a genetic algorithm. Finally, we demonstrate the practical value of both the analysis method and the optimization framework in a real-world mega-constellation case study.
item.dc:creator: Seungyeop Han, Zachary Grieser, Shoji Yoshikawa, Takumi Noro, Takumi Suda, Koki Ho

item.title: Variable Projected Augmented Lagrangian Methods for Generalized Lasso Problems
item.description: arXiv:2510.24140v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce variable projected augmented Lagrangian (VPAL) methods for solving generalized nonlinear Lasso problems with improved speed and accuracy. By eliminating the nonsmooth variable via soft-thresholding, VPAL transforms the problem into a smooth reduced formulation. We develop a preconditioned variant based on curvature-informed updates and investigate its performance for both linear and nonlinear inverse problems. We prove convergence guarantees for both standard and preconditioned VPAL under mild assumptions and show that variable projection leads to faster convergence and higher solution quality. The method seamlessly extends to nonlinear inverse problems, where it outperforms traditional approaches in applications such as phase retrieval and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging. Across linear and nonlinear imaging applications, numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy and computational efficiency of the proposed methods, highlighting the potential of variable projection for large-scale inverse problems.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Aleotti, Davide Bianchi, Florian Bossmann, Riley Yizhou Chen, Matthias Chung

item.title: Online experiment design for continuous-time systems using generalized filtering
item.description: arXiv:2511.09386v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The goal of experiment design is to select the inputs of a dynamical system in such a way that the resulting data contain sufficient information for system identification and data-driven control. This paper investigates the problem of experiment design for continuous-time systems under piecewise constant input signals. To obviate the need for measuring time derivatives of (data) trajectories, we introduce a generalized filtering framework. Our main result is to establish conditions on the input and the filter functions under which the filtered data are informative for system identification, i.e., they satisfy a certain rank condition. We assume that the filter functions are piecewise continuously differentiable, encompassing several filter functions that have appeared in the literature. Building on the proposed filtering framework, we adapt an existing experiment design procedure from discrete-time to continuous-time systems, where the piecewise constant input signal is designed online during system operation. This method is shown to be sample efficient, in the sense that it deals with the least possible number of filtered data samples for system identification. Notably, the designed input signal is such that the data capture the system's dynamics at all times between sampling instants, thus establishing a connection with a continuous-time version of Willems et al.'s fundamental lemma.
item.dc:creator: Jiwei Wang, Simone Baldi, Henk J. van Waarde

item.title: Optimal Dividend, Reinsurance and Capital-Injection Strategies for Collaborating Business Lines: The Case of Excess-of-Loss Reinsurance
item.description: arXiv:2511.11383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper considers an insurer with two collaborating business lines that must make three critical decisions: (1) dividend payout, (2) a combination of proportional and excess-of-loss reinsurance coverage, and (3) capital injection between the lines. The reserve level of each line is modeled using a diffusion approximation, and the insurer aims to maximize the weighted total discounted dividends paid until the first ruin time. We obtain the value function and the optimal strategies in explicit or semi-explicit form. We then prove that the optimal dividend payout strategy for bounded dividend rates is of threshold type, while for unbounded dividend rates it is of barrier type. Under the diffusion approximation, the optimal combination of proportional and excess-of-loss reinsurance is shown to be pure excess-of-loss reinsurance. We also show that the optimal level of risk ceded to the reinsurer decreases as the aggregate reserve level increases, and that reinsurance is phased out line by line. The optimal capital-injection strategy involves transferring reserves to prevent the ruin of one line. Finally, numerical examples are presented to illustrate these optimal strategies.
item.dc:creator: Tim J. Boonen, Engel John C. Dela Vega

item.title: A Benamou-Brenier Proximal Splitting Method for Constrained Unbalanced Optimal Transport
item.description: arXiv:2512.09250v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The dynamic formulation of optimal transport, also known as the Benamou-Brenier formulation, has been extended to the unbalanced case by introducing a source term in the continuity equation. When this source term is penalized based on the Fisher-Rao metric, the resulting model is referred to as the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) setting, and allows for the comparison between any two positive measures without the need for equalized total mass. In recent work, we introduced a constrained variant of this model, in which affine integral equality constraints are imposed along the measure path. In the present paper, we propose a further generalization of this framework, which allows for constraints that apply not just to the density path but also to the momentum and source terms, and incorporates affine inequalities in addition to equality constraints. We prove, under suitable assumptions on the constraints, the well-posedness of the resulting class of convex variational problems. The paper is then primarily devoted to developing an effective numerical pipeline that tackles the corresponding constrained optimization problem based on finite difference discretizations and parallel proximal schemes. Our proposed framework encompasses standard balanced and unbalanced optimal transport, as well as a multitude of natural and practically relevant constraints, and we highlight its versatility via several synthetic and real data examples.
item.dc:creator: Mao Nishino, Martin Bauer, Tom Needham, Nicolas Charon

item.title: Robust Parallel Machine Scheduling: A Comparison of Robustness Measures and Local Search Approaches
item.description: arXiv:2512.15471v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In many real-world scheduling problems, the processing times of tasks are subject to uncertainty. This makes it essential to design schedules that are robust against disruptions. We distinguish between two types of robustness: quality-robust schedules keep a stable objective value under disruptions, while solution-robust schedules keep a stable schedule structure. We study how to generate schedules for the Stochastic Parallel Machine Scheduling Problem (SPMSP) with precedence constraints and release dates that are both quality- and solution-robust. To this end, we compare several robustness measures and local search algorithms that use these measures. We start with an extensive simulation study where we determine the correlation of 13 existing and 6 new robustness measures with both quality and solution robustness. Next, we use the measures with high robustness correlation as the objective in our local search algorithm to find the best way to generate schedules containing both job-machine assignments as well as buffer assignments. We use a new dynamic objective weight within our local search algorithms, which actively changes the objective weights in each iteration. We found that the best way to generate robust schedules is to use robustness measures that model the processing times with normal distribution approximations and to combine job placement and buffer assignment simultaneously.
item.dc:creator: Casper Loman, Loriana Pascual, Bram Elderhorst, Marjan van den Akker, Roel van den Broek, Han Hoogeveen

item.title: High-order augmented Lagrangian methods and robust multilevel inner solvers
item.description: arXiv:2601.11826v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We analyze high-order augmented Lagrangian methods for convex optimization problems with linear constraints and construct robust multilevel inner solvers. For the high-order proximal point method, we derive energy error estimates under uniform convexity that distinguish the sublinear, linear, and superlinear regimes by comparing the regularization power with the uniform convexity exponent. Through duality, these estimates yield convergence results for the high-order augmented Lagrangian method. The primal subproblems become nearly semicoercive as the penalty parameter decreases. We address this difficulty using multilevel subspace correction methods whose subspaces decompose the constraint kernel. Applications to nonlinear diffusion, Darcy--Forchheimer flow, and the finite neuron method show how the multilevel design accommodates mean, divergence, and boundary constraints. Numerical experiments illustrate the outer convergence regimes and demonstrate parameter-robust behavior of the inner solvers across different meshes.
item.dc:creator: Young-Ju Lee, Jongho Park

item.title: Control policies for a two-stage queueing system with parallel and single server options
item.description: arXiv:2601.13576v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a two-stage queueing system attended by two flexible servers. Once a server begins to interact with a job, it remains attached to its job throughout both stages of service. After completing the first-stage service, the server chooses between two second-stage options. Option 1 sends the server-job pair to a parallel-service station where both servers may operate simultaneously; therefore, the server immediately begins the second-stage service on its job. Option 2 routes the pair to a single-service station that admits at most one server-job pair into service at a time. While we consider the complete range of parameters, the usual reason for choosing Option 2 is that jobs may receive higher-quality (faster and/or lower expected cost) service. If the single-service station is occupied, the pair must wait together until the station becomes available. The decision-making scenario is modeled via a Markov decision process formulation of a clearing system with holding costs at each station. Focusing on cases with a large initial queue, we fully characterize the structural properties of an optimal control policy based on the relationship between the service rates at the downstream stations. A numerical study highlights the significance of understanding the structure of the optimal policy by comparing its performance against several natural heuristic policies.
item.dc:creator: Shuwen Lu, Mark E. Lewis, Jamol Pender

item.title: A Bregman Regularized Proximal Point Method for Solving Equilibrium Problems on Hadamard Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2601.13959v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper we develop a Bregman regularized proximal point algorithm for solving monotone equilibrium problems on Hadamard manifolds. It has been shown that the regularization term induced by a Bregman function is, in general, nonconvex on Hadamard manifolds unless the curvature is zero. Nevertheless, we prove that the proposed Bregman regularization scheme does converge to a solution of the equilibrium problem on Hadamard manifolds in the presence of a strong assumption on the convexity of the set formed by the regularization term. Moreover, we employ a coercivity condition on the Bregman function which is weaker than those typically assumed in the existing literature on Bregman regularization. Numerical experiments on illustrative examples demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our proposed method.
item.dc:creator: Shikher Sharma, Simeon Reich

item.title: Stationary Mean-Field singular control of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process
item.description: arXiv:2601.23036v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by continuous-time optimal inventory management, we study a class of stationary mean-field control problems with singular controls. The dynamics are modeled by a mean-reverting Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, and the performance criterion is given by a quadratic long-time average expected cost functional. The mean-field dependence is through the stationary mean of the controlled process itself, which enters the ergodic cost functional. We relate optimal controls for the stationary mean-field control problem to equilibria of an associated stationary mean-field game. In particular, optimal controls induce equilibria of the associated game, while the converse holds true within the class of admissible controls satisfying an additional integrability requirement. Finally, we solve the stationary mean-field game explicitly, thereby obtaining an explicitly characterized optimal reflection policy for the stationary mean-field control problem within this restricted class.
item.dc:creator: Federico Cannerozzi

item.title: Skip the Hessian, Keep the Rates: Globalized Semismooth Newton with Lazy Hessian Updates
item.description: arXiv:2602.08069v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Second-order methods are provably faster than first-order methods, and their efficient implementations for large-scale optimization problems have attracted significant attention. Yet, optimization problems in ML often have nonsmooth derivatives, which makes the existing convergence rate theory of second-order methods inapplicable. In this paper, we propose a new semismooth Newton method (SSN) that enjoys both global convergence rates and asymptotic superlinear convergence without requiring second-order differentiability. Crucially, our method does not require (generalized) Hessians to be evaluated at each iteration but only periodically, and it reuses stale Hessians otherwise (i.e., it performs lazy Hessian updates), saving compute cost and often leading to significant speedups in time, whilst still maintaining strong global and local convergence rate guarantees. We develop our theory in an infinite-dimensional setting and illustrate it with numerical experiments on matrix factorization and neural networks with Lipschitz constraints.
item.dc:creator: Amal Alphonse, Pavel Dvurechensky, Clemens Sirotenko

item.title: A Technical Note on the Implementation and Use of PDCS
item.description: arXiv:2603.15504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This technical note documents the implementation and use of the Primal-Dual Conic Programming Solver (PDCS), a first-order solver for large-scale conic optimization problems introduced by Lin et al. (arXiv:2505.00311). It describes the algorithmic and implementation details underlying PDCS, including the restarted primal-dual hybrid gradient method framework, adaptive step-size selection, adaptive reflected Halpern iterations, adaptive restarts, and diagonal preconditioning. It also provides practical instructions for using PDCS, including its interfaces with JuMP and CVXPY, solver options, and illustrative code examples. PDCS is available at https://github.com/ZikaiXiong/PDCS under the Apache License 2.0.
item.dc:creator: Zhenwei Lin, Zikai Xiong, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye

item.title: Parallel Newton methods for the continuous quadratic knapsack problem: A Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel tale
item.description: arXiv:2603.15910v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The continuous quadratic knapsack (CQK) problem involves minimizing a diagonal convex quadratic function subject to box constraints and a single linear equality constraint. It has numerous applications in resource allocation, multicommodity flow, machine learning, and classical optimization tasks such as Lagrangian relaxation and quasi-Newton updates. In this work, we revisit the semismooth Newton method introduced by Cominetti, Mascarenhas, and Silva. We demonstrate that the method can be significantly improved in two directions. First, for projections onto the simplex or the $\ell_1$-ball, it can incorporate Condat's highly effective initial multiplier guess. Second, it can serve as a flexible foundation for CQK algorithms, allowing for different parallel variants tailored to exploit CPU and GPU computational models. These improvements are implemented in the open-source Julia package \texttt{NewtonCQK.jl}. We present extensive numerical tests comparing this implementation with other state-of-the-art solvers, demonstrating its superior efficiency and scalability.
item.dc:creator: Leonardo D. Secchin, Paulo J. S. Silva

item.title: Compactness, Regularity, and Mosco Convergence for a Radially Parametrized Subclass of $C$-GNP Domains
item.description: arXiv:2604.01813v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a radially parametrized subclass of domains satisfying the Geometric Normal Property with respect to a fixed convex core $C$ ($C$-GNP). These domains are described by a thickness function $d:\pC\to(0,\infty)$. The main contribution is the equivalence \[ \chi_{\Om_n}\to\chi_{\Om}\ \text{in }L^1 \iff d_n\to d\ \text{uniformly} \iff \Om_n\to\Om\ \text{in Hausdorff distance}. \] This equivalence is established via an explicit reconstruction formula $d(c)=\int_0^\infty \chi_{\Om}(c+t\nuC(c))\dd t$, which allows the transfer of convergence of characteristic functions into uniform convergence of geometric parameters. Thus the infinite-dimensional geometric optimization problem is reduced to the optimization of a scalar function on a fixed manifold. We prove compactness of uniformly controlled subclasses. The analysis is extended to non-connected domains with uniform separation. Under the curvature condition $\sup d<\delta_0$ (where $\delta_0$ is the normal tubular radius of $C$), we prove a conditional regularity result for the thickness function when the normal projection admits a $C^{m,\beta}$ inverse parametrization. We also give a sufficient perturbative bilipschitz condition for the radial parametrization. Using the Mosco convergence framework, we prove $\Gamma$-convergence of Dirichlet energies under domain variation for the uniformly controlled radial subclass. We also discuss the relation with the general $C$-GNP class and possible applications in shape optimization.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Barkatou

item.title: Towards Optimal Passive Feedback Control of LTI Systems under LQR Performance
item.description: arXiv:2604.14854v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study state-feedback design for continuous-time LTI systems with a control input and an external input-output pair. Our objective is to determine feedback gains that render the closed-loop system (strictly) passive with respect to the external port while minimizing the standard LQR cost in the disturbance-free case. The resulting constrained optimization problem is intractable due to bilinear matrix inequalities. We analyze the set of passivating gains, showing it is unbounded, possibly nonconvex, path-connected, and contractible. We propose an indirect approach, in which the set of passivating feedback gains is inner-approximated by a compact, convex polytope. A projected gradient flow is employed to compute a gain within this polytope that minimizes the LQR cost. Numerical examples illustrate the effectiveness of the method.
item.dc:creator: Armin Gie{\ss}ler, Pol Jan\'e-Soneira, S\"oren Hohmann

item.title: Parameterized Complexity of Stationarity Testing for Piecewise-Affine Functions and Shallow CNN Losses
item.description: arXiv:2605.10219v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the parameterized complexity of testing approximate first-order stationarity at a prescribed point for continuous piecewise-affine (PA) functions, a basic task in nonsmooth optimization. PA functions form a canonical model for nonsmooth stationarity testing and capture the local polyhedral geometry that appears in ReLU-type training losses. Recent work of Tian and So (2025) shows that testing approximate stationarity notions for PA functions is computationally intractable in the worst case, and identifies fixed-dimensional tractability as an open direction. We address this direction from the viewpoint of parameterized complexity, with the ambient dimension $d$ as the parameter. In this paper, we give XP algorithms in fixed dimension for the tractable sides, and prove W[1]-hardness for the complementary sides. Moreover, lower bounds under the parameterized $k$-Clique hypothesis rule out deterministic algorithms running in time $\rho(d)s^{o(d)}$ for any computable function $\rho$, where $s$ denotes the total binary encoding length of the instance. As a further consequence, our results yield the corresponding parameterized complexity picture for testing local minimality of continuous PA functions. We also extend our hardness results to a family of shallow ReLU CNN training losses, tested in the trainable weight space. Thus, the same parameterized-complexity picture also appears for simple CNN training losses. Notably, our lower bounds assume that $k$-Clique on $N$-vertex graphs admits no deterministic $\rho(k)N^{o(k)}$-time algorithm for any computable function $\rho$. The recent refutations of the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) (OpenAI, 2026) and the stronger fine-grained $k$-Clique hypothesis (Vassilevska Williams and Zamir, 2026) do not contradict this assumption.
item.dc:creator: Yuhan Ye

item.title: Indefinite Stochastic LQ Optimal Control for Jump-Diffusion Systems with Random Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2605.12775v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies indefinite stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control for jump-diffusion systems with random coefficients. We construct an algebraic inverse flow from the zero-control base system, extract the semimartingale kernel of the value function, and prove that it satisfies a generalized stochastic Riccati equation with jumps (SREJ). Under a uniform convexity condition, we establish the existence and uniqueness of open-loop optimal controls for any initial pair and show that the associated matrix $\mathscr{N}(t)$ is uniformly positive definite, yielding an exact closed-loop feedback representation of the optimal control via the SREJ. A distinguishing feature of our approach is that it requires neither relaxation techniques (as in the compensator method) nor additional invertibility assumptions on the optimal state process, and it accommodates the general case where the control enters the jump part ($F \neq 0$). As an application, we analyze a financial portfolio problem with a jump-diffusion risky asset whose excess return is zero, where the investor minimizes a cost functional with a negative terminal wealth weight. The uniform convexity condition reduces to an explicit inequality among the risk aversion coefficient, volatility, jump magnitude, and risk-free rate, thereby delineating the parametric region in which an optimal strategy exists. These results extend classical indefinite LQ theory to jump-diffusion systems with random coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Ma, Qingxin Meng

item.title: Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe Method: Primal-Dual Analysis, Heavy Ball Momentum, and Inexact Oracles
item.description: arXiv:2605.19828v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study projection-free optimization for convex objectives that satisfy abs-smoothness, a structural property that captures many non-smooth yet piecewise smooth functions arising, e.g., in modern machine learning models. We develop a unified framework for Abs-Smooth Frank-Wolfe methods, establishing a clean primal-dual analysis that guarantees convergence without requiring classical smoothness assumptions. Our framework extends the available results in two important directions. First, we introduce a heavy ball momentum variant and show that momentum can be incorporated naturally under abs-smoothness while preserving convergence guarantees. Second, we analyze inexact minimization oracles, demonstrating robustness to approximate inner solutions. Moreover, we relax the full convexity assumption and study the case where convexity holds only for the piecewise linear approximations of the objective, further broadening the applicability of conditional gradient methods to a wider class of non-smooth problems.
item.dc:creator: Sri Harshitha Tadinada, Sebastian Pokutta, Andrea Walther

item.title: Ces\`aro means of firmly nonexpansive iterates need not converge strongly
item.description: arXiv:2605.25491v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Firmly nonexpansive operators arise naturally as resolvents of monotone operators and as generalizations of projections and proximal mappings in convex optimization and fixed point theory. While their iterates are known to converge weakly to a fixed point, strong convergence is not guaranteed (Genel and Lindenstrauss, 1975). Strong convergence of Ces\`aro means of iterates is also known to fail for general nonlinear nonexpansive mappings (Krengel and Lin, 1987). In this paper, we show that this failure persists in the much smaller class of firmly nonexpansive mappings. Using suitable meshes, we construct a new explicit family of counterexamples in infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces with the origin as the unique fixed point. In the harmonic case, the Ces\`aro means of the iterates remain bounded away from the origin. Another variant yields Ces\`aro means that converge strongly to the origin. A third variant presents Ces\`aro means whose norms oscillate in the sense that their liminf is zero while their limsup is positive. Thus the strong convergence conclusion in von Neumann's linear mean ergodic theorem does not extend to Baillon's nonlinear mean ergodic theorem, even for firmly nonexpansive mappings.
item.dc:creator: Heinz H. Bauschke, Tran Thanh Tung

item.title: Solving Linear and Integer Programs Faster Using Data
item.description: arXiv:2605.25635v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study how much a linear program (LP) or an integer program (IP) can be compressed when solved repeatedly over a fixed feasible region with varying objective coefficients. We provide a framework that compresses LP and IP formulations with guarantees on the probability of preserving optimality, using either an uncertainty set for the cost vector or historical samples. Our framework exposes a tunable tradeoff between compression and the probability of recovering an optimal solution. We characterize the minimum dimension of affine reformulations preserving the full optimizer set over a given cost region and provide sample-based learning algorithms with fast-rate guarantees, without requiring a nondegeneracy assumption for LPs. With high confidence over the training data, the learned reformulation preserves the optimizer set for an independent test cost with probability at least $1-\rho-\widetilde{O}(d^\star_\rho/\hat n)$, where $\rho$ bounds the excluded probability mass, $d^\star_\rho$ is the retained region's decision-relevant dimension, and $\hat n$ is the number retained from $n$ training samples. Existing data-driven approaches to LP and IP reduction do not, to our knowledge, learn a single low-dimensional affine reformulation with a prescribed probability of preserving the full optimizer set. Experimental results show substantial improvements over the compared baselines in accuracy, sample efficiency, and computational speed.
item.dc:creator: Yuhan Ye, Omar Bennouna

item.title: Proper efficiency results in vector optimisation in real linear-topological spaces based on vectorial penalisation
item.description: arXiv:2605.30286v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we are dealing with constrained vector optimisation problems where the objective function acts between real linear-topological spaces. Our aim is to study the relationships between the sets of properly efficient solutions to constrained and unconstrained vector optimisation problems under certain cone convexity assumptions on the objective function using a vectorial penalisation approach.
item.dc:creator: Paul Schm\"olling, Christian G\"unther, Christiane Tammer, Elisabeth K\"obis

item.title: A stochastic gradient algorithm for non-separable optimization with convergence guarantee
item.description: arXiv:2606.10383v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study smooth parameterized non-separable objectives of the form $\mathcal L(\theta)=F(Y(\theta))$, where a global operator couples the outputs of all training samples. We analyze two stochastic gradient constructions within this output-space framework: the ideal per-batch gradient $G$, obtained by row sampling of the full output gradient, and a cached surrogate $H$ for parameterized updates in which full-data quantities are expensive to evaluate. For uniformly sampled batches, the ideal estimator has a deterministic batch-size scaling and a second moment controlled by the full output gradient. Using this structure, we establish local high-probability confinement and convergence for fixed positive step sizes on a prescribed parameter neighborhood under a power-type gradient inequality, with linear and polynomial regimes determined by its exponent. For the cached surrogate, a Lyapunov function couples the objective gap with the cache error and yields analogous local results on the corresponding non-exit event. The theory includes explicit path-length, confinement, and rate bounds; numerical experiments illustrate finite-budget decay trends and the effects of global output-gradient sampling, batch restriction, and cache tracking.
item.dc:creator: Yingzhou Li, Ruofan Wu

item.title: Maximum Utility Split Method for Utility Preference Elicitation
item.description: arXiv:2606.12868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose a new approach, called maximum utility split (MUS) scheme, which is built on random utility split (RUS) scheme but with a notable difference: one lottery is designed with two fixed outcomes but with varying probability, and the other has a deterministic outcome specifically chosen at the point where the range between the largest and smallest possible utility values is maximized. Consequently, the probability of random lottery is set such that the range of the ambiguity set of utility functions is reduced by half at the point. Under moderate conditions, we show that MUS can successively generate a sequence of such questionnaires and effectively reduce the ambiguity set, eventually converging to the true utility function as the number of questionnaires increases. The main challenge is to effectively identify the point with the largest utility range for a given ambiguity set constructed from preference information. Based on the structure of the ambiguity set, we propose an interval-based algorithm which identifies each certain-outcome lottery by solving a sequence of linear programs. Moreover, to deal with the case where elicitation terminates before the ambiguity set reduces to a singleton, we demonstrate how to figure out a nominal utility function by solving optimization programs. These identify the smallest and largest utility functions under the Kantorovich metric within the ambiguity set, after which we identify a nominal utility function located in the middle of them. Finally, numerical results demonstrate the efficiency of the MUS method and the performance of a robo-advisor system based on MUS-type queries and the nominal utility elicitation. While the main discussions focus on concave utility functions, we also demonstrate how the MUS approach can be extended to accommodate general non-concave utility functions, particularly S-shaped ones.
item.dc:creator: Bo Chen, Jia Liu, Huifu Xu

item.title: Scalable Deep Unfolding of Conic Optimizers
item.description: arXiv:2606.13825v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep unfolding (DU) accelerates iterative optimizers by training learnable components through unrolled iterations, but extending DU to the large-scale semidefinite programs (SDPs) common in robotics has remained limited. Unrolling a full-update conic solver such as COSMO exposes two obstacles: backpropagating through the per-iteration linear-system solve incurs memory quadratic in the problem size when the coefficient matrix is formed explicitly, and backpropagating through the positive semidefinite (PSD) cone projection is numerically unstable under repeated eigenvalues. We address the first with a matrix-free implicit differentiation rule that reduces memory from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n + \mathrm{nnz}(A))$, and the second with a stable backward rule based on the Dale\v{c}kii--Krein representation of the Fr\'echet derivative. Together, these enable learning lightweight hyperparameter policies and warm starts for COSMO. On standalone SDPs and second-order cone programs, ranging from max-cut and Lov\'asz $\vartheta$ to robust estimation and control, the learned policies outperform tuned COSMO on every problem class, reducing iterations to tolerance by up to 60$\times$, and transfer without retraining to instances up to 10$\times$ larger in the size parameter while retaining 2--5$\times$ speedups. Our matrix-free solver implementation also batches naturally on the GPU, solving 64 Lov\'asz $\vartheta$ SDPs 14$\times$ faster than sequential COSMO.jl. When embedded in sequential convex programming for nonlinear covariance steering, our learned optimizers outperform the interior-point solver Clarabel in terms of both success rate and solve time.
item.dc:creator: Alex Oshin, Rahul Vodeb Ghosh, Evangelos A. Theodorou

item.title: Discrete Coplanarity Rigidity and Local Mahler Volume Growth Near the Cube
item.description: arXiv:2606.14709v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the finite-dimensional isovertex radial stratum of the cube, P(c)=conv{(1+c_q)q : q in Q_n={+/-1}^n}, with c(-q)=c(q), and establish quantitative rigidity and volume-product estimates for n>=3. The first main result identifies the kernel of the linearized facet-coplanarity operator R_n with the homothety direction span{1} and proves that the coplanarity defect is locally equivalent to both the transverse amplitude dist_infty(c,span{1}) and the distance d_GL(P(c),C_n) to the GL(n)-orbit of the cube. After normalizing out the homothety mode onto 1^perp, a key step is a second-order comparison between the linearized vertex-displacement seminorm and its optimization over small linear transformations. The second main result converts transverse radial perturbations c in 1^perp into a linear volume increment. A facetwise concave-envelope construction and an associated pocket functional yield the explicit primal lower bound vol(P(c))-2^n >= 8/(3(n-1))||c||_infty - O(||c||_infty^2) on 1^perp. Combining this with a chamber-independent first-order expansion of the polar volume (whose linear part vanishes on 1^perp with a uniform quadratic remainder) gives a linear lower bound for the Mahler product V_M(P(c))-V_M(C_n) in terms of d_GL(P(c),C_n). In dimension three, an exact chamber analysis on 1^perp yields vol(P(c))=8+(8/3)||c||_infty+O(||c||_infty^2), and the Mahler product has one-sided directional derivative (32/9)||u||_infty along every nonzero ray in 1^perp. In dimension four, a symmetry-orbit classification of the seventy balanced Boolean directions yields six combinatorial types and explicit first-order pocket bounds. We also distinguish the frozen-combinatorics KKT balance from geometric stationarity.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Mart\'in Jim\'enez Cuevas

item.title: Optimizing the Principal Coefficient of Elliptic Equations using $L^p$-regularity, $p < \infty$
item.description: arXiv:2606.17788v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study coefficient identification problems for elliptic partial differential equations with total variation regularization and control constraints. Existing related literature relies on continuity and differentiability properties of the control-to-state operator with respect to the $L^\infty$-norm. While this is sufficient for deriving optimality conditions, it is not well-suited for numerical algorithms, as it neglects the spatial extent of perturbations and leads to a qualitative discrepancy compared to $L^q$-norms with $q < \infty$. In this work, we address this gap by exploiting $W^{1,s}$-regularity results to establish differentiability properties of the control-to-state operator with respect to $L^q$-norms for finite $q$. Based on this framework, we derive first- and second-order differentiability results for the reduced objective functional and establish first-order optimality conditions involving a restricted subdifferential characterization of the total variation seminorm and corresponding regularity of the associated multipliers. Building on this, we analyze a nonsmooth trust-region method based on an $L^r$-trust region for $r > 0.5 q$ and prove its convergence to first-order stationary points.
item.dc:creator: Ala' Alalabi, Lorena Bociu, Paul Manns

item.title: Preference-Based Reward Learning under Partial Observability with Inexact Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2606.30271v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study how partial observability and inexact latent-state inference affect reward learning from preferences. To that end, we study preference-based reward learning under partial observability, where the learner forms latent-state estimates using an inexact learned POMDP model, so model error can accumulate over time. For finite log-linear POMDPs, we characterize this error term by establishing the stability of the belief filter to parametric model error under certain mixing conditions, yielding bounds on the belief mismatch in expectation and in high probability. We further extend this stability mechanism beyond the log-linear setting to neural-softmax POMDP models with overparameterized neural networks. We then propagate these errors into trajectory-level feature perturbations and derive finite-sample guarantees for constrained Bradley-Terry reward estimation from preferences. Our results decouple statistical error from an irreducible model-mismatch bias, and clarify when preference-based reward learning remains feasible under partial observability with imperfect dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Reza Zolnouri, Semih Cayci

item.title: Uniform Exponential Stability Analysis of Impulsive Linear Time-Invariant Systems on Banach and Hilbert Spaces: Non-Coercive and Coercive Stability Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2607.17260v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the uniform exponential stability analysis of infinite-dimensional impulsive systems defined on a Banach or Hilbert space, whose flow is governed by a fixed $C_0$-semigroup generator and whose jumps occur at a prescribed time sequence. While the flow and jump maps are themselves time-invariant, the time-triggered impulses render the propagator a genuinely time-varying evolution family, which is the source of the analysis difficulty addressed here. We combine ideas from hybrid systems theory and infinite-dimensional systems to produce operator-based stability conditions, which can be analytically or numerically checked via convex programming. Necessary and sufficient conditions for the uniform exponential stability of impulsive systems on Banach spaces are obtained in the context of a fixed impulse-times sequence but also of arbitrary, constant, minimum, and range dwell-times using both non-coercive and coercive Lyapunov functionals. Some of those results are then adapted to systems on a Hilbert space and quadratic Lyapunov functionals. As an application, linear switched systems are shown to be an exact special case: reformulated as impulsive systems with unit-norm selector jumps, they inherit non-coercive and clock-dependent dwell-time stability conditions on both Banach and Hilbert spaces. Theoretical and numerical examples are given for illustration, notably on the sampled-data control of time-delay systems.
item.dc:creator: Corentin Briat, Francesco Ferrante, Christophe Prieur

item.title: The complexity landscape of robust (integer) linear programming
item.description: arXiv:2608.21574v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the computational complexity of the decision versions of three classic classes of robust optimization problems: static robust optimization, two-stage (adjustable) robust optimization, and $K$-adaptability. We consider that the feasibility sets, the uncertainty sets, and the recourse sets are polyhedra or integer-programming-representable sets, the uncertainty is decision-independent or decision-dependent, and the feasible regions are bounded or unbounded. While these problems are well-established in the current literature, we give a systematic classification that places them in the complexity classes $\mathsf{P}$, $\mathsf{NP}$, $\mathsf{coNP}$, and higher levels of the polynomial hierarchy ($\Sigma_2^p$ and $\Sigma_3^p$), and, once decision-dependent uncertainty introduces quadratic constraints, in the existential theory of the reals and its hierarchy ($\exists\mathbb{R}$, $\Sigma_2\mathbb{R}$, and $\Sigma_3\mathbb{R}$) or among the undecidable problems. Beyond hardness reductions, we pay particular attention to membership proofs, establishing polynomial-size certificates even though the sets considered generally contain vectors of exponential encoding length. As a by-product, we give an alternative proof that bilevel linear optimization lies in $\mathsf{NP}$, exploiting its connection to decision-dependent robust optimization. For $K$-adaptability, we relate the problem to its static and two-stage counterparts, showing that hardness grows monotonically with $K$ and that, for fully discrete decision-dependent instances, $K$-adaptability reduces back to the static problem.
item.dc:creator: Michael Poss, Jannis Kurtz, Marc Goerigk, Dorothee Henke

item.title: Accelerated primal-dual dynamical systems for convex optimization with nonlinear inequality constraints
item.description: arXiv:2609.01415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we propose accelerated inertial primal-dual dynamics for convex optimization problems with nonlinear convex inequality constraints. The proposed dynamics combine Nesterov accelerated vanishing damping $\alpha/t$, a projected augmented-Lagrangian multiplier, and tangent extrapolation of the constraint mapping. Without assuming strong convexity, we establish global well-posedness and simultaneous $\mathcal O(t^{-2})$ decay rates for the constraint violation and the objective residual when $\alpha\geq3$ and the extrapolation parameter satisfies a suitable compatibility condition. Under stricter parameter conditions, with $\alpha>3$, we further prove that the primal-dual trajectory converges to a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker pair, both residuals decay as $o(t^{-2})$. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Xin He

item.title: Equilibria for Time-inconsistent Regular-singular Control Problems with Non-exponential Discount
item.description: arXiv:2609.08877v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies a time-inconsistent mixed regular-singular control problem in continuous time with non-exponential discount. We seek time-consistent equilibria in an intrapersonal game framework and propose two novel definitions of regular-singular equilibrium where both regular and singular controls are unified via control laws. The standard equilibrium definition allows simultaneous perturbations of both controls, while a mild definition restricts perturbations to one control at a time. Verification theorems providing sufficient conditions are established for both definitions. We illustrate the applicability of the theory through the effort and dividend problem. First, a mild equilibrium is constructed, yet not a standard equilibrium, highlighting the distinction between the two definitions. Moreover, we derive semi-explicit threshold-type equilibria under both a mixture of exponential discount functions and a pseudo-exponential discount function. In both cases, the convexity of the value function is rigorously established, the equilibrium conditions are verified, and the existence of the effort and dividend thresholds is proved. Numerical results reveal the impacts of exogenous parameters on the effort and dividend thresholds and the equilibrium value function, along with their economic implications.
item.dc:creator: Yuting Jia, Zongxia Liang, Xiaodong Luo

item.title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
item.description: arXiv:2609.09108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large linear programs can exceed the memory of a single compute node. Although first-order methods replace sparse factorizations with GPU-suited matrix-vector products, other solver phases can reintroduce a single-node memory limit. We present SHARDLP, a distributed GPU LP solver that keeps the matrix and primal-dual state partitioned from sharded input through solution output. On the Google PDLP benchmark, SHARDLP solves ten of eleven instances, compared with eight in the published CPU PDLP study. On the largest benchmark, eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185-billion-variable, 6.338-billion-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; the published CPU experiment reports 21.06 hours on different hardware. Beyond this benchmark, separately checked multi-node solves reach up to 13.604 billion variables and 40.807 billion nonzeros, while validated executions span up to 76 GPUs across 29 compute nodes. For column-partitioned solves, support-aware communication skips GPUs that store no coefficients for a row; on an LP with 2.76 billion nonzeros, it cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. The code for SHARDLP is available at https://github.com/ArnaudDeza/ShardLP.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Deza, Santanu S. Dey, Pascal Van Hentenryck

item.title: A global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with quadratic convex generator and unbounded terminal condition
item.description: arXiv:2609.21451v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a global stochastic maximum principle for forward-backward stochastic control systems with an unbounded terminal condition and a generator that has quadratic growth and is convex in $Z$. The control domain need not be convex, and the diffusion coefficient may depend on the control. In this setting, the BMO martingale estimates used for quadratic BSDEs with bounded terminal conditions are no longer directly available. To overcome this difficulty, we work under an equivalent probability measure associated with the optimal trajectory and establish the estimates needed for the variational analysis. In particular, using a representation formula for convex quadratic BSDEs with conditional estimates, we derive estimates for the backward-state perturbations under this fixed measure. These estimates allow us to justify a second-order expansion of the cost functional and obtain the global stochastic maximum principle.
item.dc:creator: Ying Hu, Feng Li, Jiaqiang Wen

item.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
item.description: arXiv:2609.30212v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize, up to logarithmic factors, the optimal higher-order oracle complexity of finding approximate solutions to composite monotone inclusion problems, formed by the sum of a smooth single-valued monotone operator and a maximal monotone set-valued operator. We introduce the Anchored Extra-Proximal (AEP) framework, which combines an anchored extrapolation step with an inexact anchored proximal update satisfying a relative-error condition. This framework recovers the composite Fast Extragradient method in the first-order setting and yields natural higher-order extensions through Taylor approximations of the smooth operator at the extrapolated point. For every $p\geq 2$, assuming that the $(p-1)$th derivative of the single-valued operator is $L_p$-Lipschitz continuous and the initial distance to a solution is at most $R$, we combine AEP with a bisection line search to obtain a $p$th-order method that attains a tangent residual of at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}((L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ oracle calls. We complement this result with a worst-case lower bound of $\Omega((L_p R^p/\varepsilon)^{\frac{2}{3p-1}})$ for every deterministic algorithm in the $p$th-order oracle model, without imposing any prescribed update structure. For the subclass of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems, we further establish a lower bound of $\Omega(\min\{R/\varepsilon, {(L_p R^{p}/\varepsilon)}^{\frac{2}{3p-1}}\})$. By choosing between AEP and Halpern iteration, we match this lower bound up to logarithmic factors, thereby also settling the deterministic oracle complexity of smooth nonexpansive fixed-point problems.
item.dc:creator: Ruichen Jiang, TaeHo Yoon

item.title: Feedback Stabilization for Sampled Linear Systems with Control-linear Noise
item.description: arXiv:2609.30438v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider linear stochastic systems with control-linear noise and periodically sampled measurements. We address the problem of feedback stabilization in the mean-square sense. The main contribution of the paper is to provide a necessary and sufficient condition for feedback stabilization. In particular, we relate feedback stabilizability of the stochastic system to the existence of a fixed point of a Riccati-type algebraic equation and, further, to the existence of a solution to an infinite-horizon optimal control problem.
item.dc:creator: Cynthia Cheng, Xudong Chen

item.title: Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Reinforcement Learning for Derivative-Free Model-Based Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.18524v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Optimal control problems become computationally challenging when the system dynamics are nonsmooth, learned from data, or available only through a simulator. In such settings, derivatives may be difficult to obtain, and evaluating different control actions through repeated trajectory simulations can be expensive. We propose Hamiltonian Primal-Dual Policy Optimization (HPDPO), a method that uses numerical costates to guide the search for improved controls. The costates are estimated using finite differences of the numerical model and are used to rank candidate actions. Rather than performing a full remaining-horizon simulation for every candidate, HPDPO evaluates a small set of promising alternatives and accepts a control update only when it decreases the discrete objective. We derive a first-order costate-based approximation for ranking candidate actions and establish descent of the discretized objective under rollout-verified updates. We test the method on scalar and multidimensional control problems, including examples with nonsmooth and learned dynamics. The results show good agreement with analytical or published reference solutions and lower simulation costs than the direct-rollout methods considered. HPDPO requires only forward model evaluations, without analytical or automatically differentiated derivatives of the dynamics or a learned value function.
item.dc:creator: K. Rabiei, Z. Rui, X. Lu, W. Hao

item.title: A Retrospective-Approximation Interior-Point Method
item.description: arXiv:2610.38857v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An algorithm is proposed, analyzed, and tested for solving nonlinearly constrained continuous optimization problem instances wherein the objective function is defined by an expectation over a random variable argument and the constraints include inequalities (and perhaps equalities) involving functions that may be nonconvex. The algorithm combines a retrospective-approximation strategy for handling the objective and an interior-point approach for handling the constraints. In each iteration of an outer loop, the objective is approximated by an empirical average over a set of realizations of the random variable argument and the resulting sampled problem is solved with an interior-point method that allows inexact search-direction computations for computational flexibility. Termination conditions for the interior-point method are tailored for those needed for convergence guarantees by the outer loop. Over the outer loop, the sample set is updated adaptively in such a manner that convergence guarantees for solving the original optimization problem can be assured. The results of numerical experiments are presented, which show that the proposed algorithm can outperform competing methods that have comparable theoretical guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Frank E. Curtis, Zahra Khatti, Daniel P. Robinson

item.title: Multi-rate high-order regularization with an order-$(p-2)$ oracle
item.description:
arXiv:2611.01819v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider unconstrained minimization of a possibly nonconvex function $f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}$ whose $p$th derivative is Lipschitz continuous, with $p\geq3$, when derivative information is available only through order $p-2$. The unavailable tensors $
abla^{p-1}f$ and $
abla^pf$ are reconstructed from central finite differences of $
abla^{p-2}f$. Since the two reconstructions have different point-query costs, we use a block length $m$ for the order-$p$ approximation and a subblock length $\ell\leq m$ for the order-$(p-1)$ approximation. The latter is transported between consecutive reconstruction points using the stored order-$p$ approximation. This leads to an adaptive regularization method that does not require prior knowledge of the Lipschitz constant. We prove finite termination at an $\epsilon$-approximate first-order stationary point and derive an explicit bound on the number of bundled order-$(p-2)$ oracle queries. For $m=(p-2)n^2$ and $\ell=(p-2)n$, the accuracy-dependent term has dimension--accuracy scaling $n^{3/p}\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$. Thus the method retains the $\epsilon^{-(p+1)/p}$ dependence of full order-$p$ regularization while using derivatives only through order $p-2$. Within the dense reconstruction framework considered here, using separate block and subblock lengths gives dimension dependence of order $n^{3/p}$, compared with $n^{4/p}$ when a common length is imposed.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Kabgani

item.title: Conditions for Normality of Pontryagin's Maximum Principle in the Absence of State Constraints
item.description: arXiv:2611.05743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Pontryagin's Maximum Principle is said to be "normal" for the problem at hand when it has a solution (maximizer u*) that explicitly involves the problem's cost function, making the maximum principle helpful (while in the opposite situation it is of no help). The aim of the present paper is, for Lagrange optimal control problems without state constraints, to identify classes of problems for which the Principle is normal. General conditions are introduced that guarantee normality, and classes of problems that satisfy these conditions are identified. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the control values) "augmented" reachable set, with cost along an upward vertical axis, has a convex lower-boundary function and the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the reachable state set, with the terminal constraint within the affine hull of that set. Such classes include problems for which the constrained (by bounds on the values of the control signal) "augmented" (with the cost value along an upward "vertical axis") reachable set has a "convex" lower boundary for which the optimal terminal state lies in the relative interior of the set of reachable states. Special attention is given to Lagrange steering problems: sufficient conditions are obtained on a nested sequence of sub-classes of such problems, culminating with the class of steering problems with scalar control signal and linear time-invariant (LTI) state dynamics and objective integrand, for which normality is guaranteed whenever all eigenvalues of the state dynamics matrix A are real (e.g., if A is symmetric or triangular or the system is overdamped) or have small enough imaginary parts; simple 2 x 2 examples show that, in contrast with the situation in the finite-dimensional case, this property does not extend to arbitrary A matrices.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Tits, Pierre-Antoine Absil, No\'e Tits

item.title: The Convergence Rate of Accelerated Proximal Gradient Methods with General Inertial Term for Convex Composite Multiobjective Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2611.06125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods with general stepsizes for convex composite multiobjective optimization, where each objective is a smooth convex term plus a proper closed convex term and the proximal subproblem keeps a separate offset for each objective. For a two-parameter root momentum rule with trajectory-dependent coefficients, we construct a new energy function and establish an energy identity. This yields sharper convergence guarantees: boundedness, weighted square summability of the displacements, a merit-function rate of $o(k^{-2})$, and displacement decay of $o(k^{-1})$ whenever the first parameter converges to a value in $(0,1)$; the second parameter need not converge or have bounded total variation. At the critical value $\alpha=3$, we obtain $u_0(x^N)\le \frac{2\ell R}{N(N+3)},$ together with $O(1/N)$ displacement decay, square summability, and weak Pareto convergence. The remaining little-$o$ question at $\alpha=3$ is reduced to the vanishing of a nonnegative critical energy. For $1<\alpha<3$, we prove the rate $O(N^{-(\alpha-1)})$, and for every $\alpha>0$ we obtain $u_0(x^k)\to0$, $F_i(x^k)\to c_i$, and $\sum_k D_k/k<\infty$. A JOS1 experiment numerically validates the predicted little-$o$ separation and the rate behavior.
item.dc:creator: Chengzhi Huang

item.title: Technical Report: Partially Asynchronous Distributed Optimization on Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2611.06722v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: There is a large body of work on distributed optimization for problems in Euclidean space. However, many existing algorithms and analyses do not directly transfer to problems defined on manifolds. Therefore, in this paper we propose a distributed asynchronous optimization algorithm for problems on Riemannian manifolds. The algorithm we develop is a parallelized form of Riemannian block coordinate descent in which all agents can compute and communicate asynchronously. We assume only "partial asynchrony", namely that all delays in computations and communications obey some finite bound, and we omit the common assumptions of convexity of the objective and compactness of the manifold. Under mild conditions, we prove that agents' iterates drive the Riemannian gradient of the objective to zero, and we derive a rate of convergence for the norm of the gradient. In simulations, we compare to a synchronous baseline algorithm under varying communication delays and numbers of agents. In example problems, we empirically show that our algorithm converges up to 8.5 times faster and attains up to 24 times lower suboptimality over a finite horizon.
item.dc:creator: Adam Pooley, William Warke, Matthew T. Hale

item.title: Minimum-Time Interceptor Selection and Obstacle-Avoiding Path Planning for Heterogeneous UAVs
item.description: arXiv:2611.07279v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Selecting the most suitable unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to intercept a moving target is challenging when multiple vehicles have different speeds, initial headings, turning capabilities and launch delays, particularly in environments containing obstacles. This paper develops a computationally efficient framework that integrates minimum-time interceptor selection with obstacle-avoiding path planning for heterogeneous UAVs. The interception problem for each UAV is formulated as a minimum-time optimal control problem and solved numerically using an arc-parameterised nonlinear programming model based on Dubins-type paths. The candidate trajectories consist of minimum-radius circular arcs, straight-line segments and tangential obstacle-boundary arcs, with exact geometric distance constraints imposed to ensure obstacle avoidance along the entire path. To improve computational efficiency, a closed-form lower bound on interception time is incorporated into a bound-and-select algorithm that eliminates UAVs unable to improve the best verified feasible interception time. The proposed pruning strategy preserves the best computed interception decision obtained through full enumeration while reducing computational effort. Numerical experiments investigate the effects of target speed, UAV turning radius, launch delay and obstacle configuration. Across 20 randomly generated scenarios involving up to eight UAVs, the proposed approach reduces average computational time by approximately 85$\%$ for eight-vehicle teams without changing the selected interceptor or its computed interception time. The proposed approach provides an efficient method for selecting a single UAV and generating feasible Dubins-type interception trajectories in obstacle-constrained environments.
item.dc:creator: M. M. Rizvi, Masuda Akter

item.title: Convergence Analysis of an Upwind Finite-Difference Scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman Equations
item.description: arXiv:2301.06415v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the convergence of an upwind finite-difference scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations on a one-dimensional periodic domain, considering both the value function and the feedback control selected by the discrete pointwise minimization. For classical value functions whose time and spatial derivatives are H\"older continuous in their respective variables, we bound the error at the grid points by a constant times the sum of the time step and spatial mesh width each raised to their common H\"older exponent. This yields first-order convergence when these derivatives are Lipschitz continuous and the meshes are refined proportionally. Under additional spatial regularity of the problem data, we also prove convergence of both one-sided difference quotients of the discrete value function to the spatial derivative of the value function: the integral over space and time of the absolute error tends to zero for each difference quotient. We further establish convergence of the discrete controls to the continuous feedback control when the continuous pointwise minimizer is unique, regardless of how the discrete minimizers are selected. These theoretical results are supported by numerical experiments that illustrate the accuracy of the value-function approximation and the behavior of the computed feedback controls.
item.dc:creator: Daisuke Inoue, Nao Hamamuki, Yuji Ito, Takahito Kashiwabara, Norikazu Saito, Hiroaki Yoshida

item.title: Sample-Efficient Quantum State Tomography for Structured Quantum States in One Dimension
item.description: arXiv:2410.02583v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we answer this fundamental question affirmatively by using a class of informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (IC-POVMs), including symmetric IC-POVMs (SIC-POVMs) and spherical $t$-designs, focusing on sample complexity while not accounting for the implementation complexity of the measurement settings. For SIC-POVMs and spherical 2-designs, we show that the number of state copies to guarantee bounded recovery error of an MPO state with a constrained least-squares estimator depends on the probability distribution of the MPO under the POVM but scales only linearly with $n$ when the distribution is approximately uniform. For general spherical $t$-designs with a sufficiently large $t$, we prove that only a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is sufficient for a guaranteed recovery of any state represented by an MPO. In addition, we establish a sample complexity lower bound based on the Cramer-Rao bound, showing that, for strictly positive definite MPO states and unbiased estimators, a number of state copies proportional to the number of independent parameters in the MPO is also necessary, although the upper and lower bounds do not yet match in their dependence on the target accuracy. Furthermore, we propose a spectral method and a projected gradient descent (PGD) algorithm to solve the constrained least-squares problem, both equipped with rigorous recovery error guarantees.
item.dc:creator: Zhen Qin, Casey Jameson, Alireza Goldar, Michael B. Wakin, Zhexuan Gong, Zhihui Zhu

item.title: Guaranteed Noisy CP Tensor Recovery via Riemannian Optimization on the Segre Manifold
item.description: arXiv:2510.00569v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering a low-CP-rank tensor from noisy linear measurements is a central challenge in high-dimensional data analysis, with applications spanning tensor PCA, scalar-on-tensor regression, tensor-on-tensor regression, and beyond. We exploit the intrinsic geometry of rank-one tensors by casting the recovery task as an optimization problem over the Segre manifold, the smooth Riemannian manifold of rank-one tensors. This geometric viewpoint yields two powerful algorithms: Riemannian Gradient Descent (RGD) and Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN), each of which preserves feasibility at every iteration. Under mild noise assumptions, we prove that RGD converges at a local linear rate, while RGN exhibits an initial local quadratic phase followed by linear refinement to the statistical error. Extensive synthetic experiments validate these convergence guarantees and demonstrate the practical effectiveness of our methods.
item.dc:creator: Ke Xu, Yuefeng Han

item.title: Convergence of optimizers implies eigenvalues filtering at equilibrium
item.description: arXiv:2510.09034v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ample empirical evidence in deep neural network training suggests that a variety of optimizers tend to find nearly global optima. In this article, we adopt the reversed perspective that convergence to an arbitrary point is assumed rather than proven, focusing on the consequences of this assumption. From this viewpoint, in line with recent advances on the edge-of-stability phenomenon, we argue that different optimizers effectively act as eigenvalue filters determined by their hyperparameters. Specifically, the standard gradient descent method inherently avoids the sharpest minima, whereas Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM) algorithms go even further by actively favoring wider basins. Inspired by these insights, we propose two novel algorithms that exhibit enhanced eigenvalue filtering, effectively promoting wider minima. Our theoretical analysis leverages a generalized Hadamard--Perron stable manifold theorem and applies to general semialgebraic $C^2$ functions, without requiring additional non-degeneracy conditions or global Lipschitz bound assumptions. We support our conclusions with numerical experiments on feed-forward neural networks.
item.dc:creator: Jerome Bolte (TSE-R), Quoc-Tung Le (DAO), Edouard Pauwels (TSE-R)

item.title: On fractal minimizers and potentials of occupation measures
item.description: arXiv:2512.14248v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We highlight two basic types of variational problems and prove the existence of fractal minimizers through the direct method in the calculus of variations. By design these minimizers are H\"older curves or H\"older parametrizations of surfaces whose images generally have a non-integer Hausdorff dimension. Their origin is deterministic, but their regularity properties are roughly similar to those of typical realizations of stochastic processes. As a key tool and our main technical result, we prove novel continuity and boundedness results for potentials of occupation measures of Gaussian random fields. These results complement well-known results for local times, but hold under much less restrictive assumptions. In an auxiliary section, we generalize earlier results on nonlinear compositions of fractional Sobolev functions with $BV$-functions to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hinz, Jonas M. T\"olle, Lauri Viitasaari

item.title: Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Nonlinear Matrix Decompositions
item.description: arXiv:2512.17473v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an algorithm based on the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) for solving nonlinear matrix decompositions (NMD). Given an input matrix $X \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$ and a factorization rank $r \ll \min(m, n)$, NMD seeks matrices $W \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times r}$ and $H \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times n}$ such that $X \approx f(WH)$, where $f$ is an element-wise nonlinear function. We evaluate our method on several representative nonlinear models: the rectified linear unit activation $f(x) = \max(0, x)$, suitable for nonnegative sparse data approximation, the component-wise square $f(x) = x^2$, applicable to probabilistic circuit representation, and the MinMax transform $f(x) = \min(b, \max(a, x))$, relevant for recommender systems. The proposed framework flexibly supports diverse loss functions, including least squares, $\ell_1$ norm, and the Kullback-Leibler divergence, and can be readily extended to other nonlinearities and metrics. We illustrate the applicability, efficiency, and adaptability of the approach on real-world datasets, highlighting its potential for a broad range of applications.
item.dc:creator: Atharva Awari, Nicolas Gillis, Arnaud Vandaele

item.title: All-Pass Function OPF: A Solver-Friendly, Physics-Preserving Approximation of AC OPF
item.description: arXiv:2601.14468v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper presents a rational approximation of the AC optimal power flow (AC OPF) problem based on an all-pass approximation of the exponential power flow kernel. The classical AC OPF relies on trigonometric coupling between bus voltage phasors, which yields a nonconvex program with oscillatory derivatives that can slow, or in some cases destabilize, interior-point methods. We replace the trigonometric terms with an all-pass function (APF) approximation whose real and imaginary components act as smooth surrogates for the cosine and sine functions, and we introduce a pre-rotation to shift the argument of the approximation toward its most accurate region, ensuring that the reformulated power flow model preserves physical loss behavior, maintains the symmetry of the classical kernels, and improves the conditioning of the Jacobian and Hessian matrices. The proposed APF OPF formulation remains nonconvex, as in the classical model, but it eliminates trigonometric evaluations and empirically produces larger and more stable Newton steps under standard interior-point solvers. Numerical results on more than 25 IEEE and PGLib test systems ranging from 9 to 10{,}000 buses demonstrate that the APF OPF model achieves solutions with accuracy comparable to that of the classical formulation while reducing solver times, indicating a more solver-friendly nonconvex representation of AC OPF. All code, functions, verification scripts, and generated results are publicly available on \href{https://github.com/LSU-RAISE-LAB/APF-OPF}{GitHub}, along with a README describing how to run and reproduce the experiments.
item.dc:creator: Milad Hasanzadeh, Amin Kargarian, Javad Lavaei

item.title: Monotone Optimisation with Learned Projections
item.description: arXiv:2601.20983v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Optimisation algorithms typically assume oracle access to objectives and constraints, yet in many applications these functions are available only through data. To recover them, a common approach learns a surrogate for each function and optimises over it, but this can be unnecessarily expensive and may fail to preserve the structure required by the optimisation algorithm. We study this problem for monotone optimisation, a class of non-convex problems which can be solved globally using the Polyblock Outer Approximation (POA) algorithm. Our key observation is that POA does not require the constraint functions themselves, but only a scalar quantity we call the radial inverse. Learning this quantity directly replaces POA's inner bisection loop over a learned constraint with a single radial inverse evaluation. We characterise exactly which maps arise as radial inverses of monotone constraints, and relate their approximation error to perturbations of the feasible set and optimal objective value. Building on these results, we introduce Homogeneous-Monotone Radial Inverse (HM-RI) networks, structured min-max models that enforce the monotonicity and positive-homogeneity of radial inverses by construction. Across synthetic monotone optimisation problems and a cellular transmit-power application, HM-RI improves solution quality over direct constraint surrogates and local optimisation baselines by up to 58.6 percentage points relative to the Oracle reference objective, while achieving a 3.0-4.7x speed-up over bisection-based POA with learned constraint surrogates, with the largest solution-quality gains occurring in data-limited and piecewise-constant settings.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Rashwan, Keith Briggs, Chris Budd, Lisa Kreusser

item.title: Soft-Radial Projection for Constrained End-to-End Learning
item.description: arXiv:2602.03461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Constrained end-to-end learning trains neural networks whose outputs must satisfy feasibility constraints, such as resource, budget, or operational limits. While projection and optimization layers guarantee constraint satisfaction, boundary-based projections can introduce unfavorable optimization geometry: regions of the unconstrained output space are mapped to the same active face of the feasible set. This makes the resulting map locally rank-deficient, suppressing gradients in constrained directions and potentially impairing optimization - a bottleneck known as gradient saturation. We propose Soft-Radial Projection (SRP), a differentiable reparameterization layer that maps unconstrained network outputs into the relative interior of a convex feasible set by smoothly rescaling rays from a strictly feasible anchor point. Unlike hard radial or orthogonal projections, the resulting map is one-to-one and has a full-rank Jacobian almost everywhere, while guaranteeing strict feasibility.
